stem:
Last year the mean time for pizza deliveries from Pete’s Pizza Pit was 32.4 minutes. This year the time, $t$ minutes, for pizza deliveries from Pete’s Pizza Pit was recorded for a random sample of 50 deliveries. The results were as follows.

$$n = 50 \qquad \sum t = 1700 \qquad \sum t^2 = 59\,050$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find unbiased estimates of the population mean and variance.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Test, at the 2% significance level, whether the mean delivery time has changed since last year.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Under what circumstances would it **not** be necessary to use the Central Limit Theorem in answering **(b)**?
